comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject audited refunds even when history is missing**

When an already-migrated overcap save has `echoCreditAuditVersion: 1` but loses both its `node.echo` receipt and `history.echo`, this guard is skipped because it requires the history objects to exist. Execution then reaches the refund path and credits the entire original-value refund again—for example, a level-7 save with 33 Prisms becomes 49 instead of selecting recovery. Treat the audit version plus `raw > 6` as sufficient evidence that a missing receipt is invalid, regardless of whether history also survived.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L64-L67](https://github.com/karahaNx/Lumenfall/blob/4ef0608988e9d809f5214857192e48ae95aba4d5/AGENTS.md#L64-L67)

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid overflowing the Echo receipt tolerance**

For overcap saves containing purchase index 2085 or later, `value` is still finite but the intermediate `value * level` overflows, making `allowance` infinite and the stored validation bounds `[-Infinity, Infinity]`. Consequently, any positive finite integer in that suffix of `receipt.amounts.prisms` is accepted rather than selecting recovery (for example, a raw-2100 receipt still canonicalizes after its final price is changed to `1`). Compute the relative-error factor before multiplying by `value`, as the Recruitment implementation does, so damaged high-level receipts cannot silently pass validation.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L64-L67](https://github.com/karahaNx/Lumenfall/blob/3ad4751c683938313f0bed7c8e612dd76a9b3bbb/AGENTS.md#L64-L67)

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Canonicalize Echo refunds across JavaScript engines**

When the same unrefunded overcap save is first loaded on different supported JavaScript engines, this runtime `Math.pow` calculation produces different refund amounts. The committed compatibility fixture demonstrates that V8 6 and modern V8 diverge beginning at index 93; by raw level 95, the otherwise identical save receives two fewer Prisms on the legacy engine, with much larger absolute divergence at higher levels. Receipt tolerance preserves an already-migrated value but does not make the initial migration deterministic, so derive new receipts from one canonical price schedule rather than the host engine's `Math.pow` result.
